items.t: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
items.sum: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

items.t: Democrats try out a strange new emotion at post-midterms What's Next conference: hope
items.sum: Democrats spent two days chewing over their future at the What's Next conference and trying to deal with the fact that it looks, for a moment at least, quite bright.

items.t: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins becomes first Democrat since 1998 elected governor in Alaska
items.sum: His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

items.t: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
items.sum: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

items.t: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
items.sum: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.

items.t: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
items.sum: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

items.t: Brooks and Marcus on how Republicans are responding to midterm losses
items.sum: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Ruth Marcus of The New Yorker join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and what the Trump administration knew, how...

items.t: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado loses U.S. House seat to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
items.sum: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Rep. Lauren Boebert for a Colorado U.S. House seat on Friday, ousting a three-term Republican and staple of conservative media.

items.t: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
items.sum: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in...
